summary.fallback: Find the outpost witness, hear what happened, then decide whether truth is worth sparing a raider.

offer_line.fallback: The trail points back toward the outpost. One raider remained behind after the night our hero keeps describing. Find him before someone else silences him.

target_line.fallback: Easy now... I know that look. You did not come all this way just to hear me beg, did you?

talk.fallback: Were you there when the villagers were attacked?
Aye. I saw your village champion too. Not fighting. Kneeling. Paying us to leave him alive.
He bought his own life with theirs. One guard stayed behind so the others could run. Your hero took the guard's medal from the mud after we were done laughing.
Because liars ask for gold. I am asking to walk away with my breath. Spare me, and I will tell you where he hid the dead guard's things.

attack_choice_label.fallback: You are a raider. Your word dies with you.

spare_choice_label.fallback: Speak, then leave this village's roads.

attack_return_line.fallback: The witness is dead? Then the only man left with a story is the one wearing the medal. That is convenient. Too convenient.

spared_line.fallback: You are letting me live? Then listen close, because I will only buy my breath once.

post_spare_line.fallback: The old guard's proof is buried under loose stone near the outpost road. His sword, a few pages, and a strip of blue village cloth. Your hero hid them there because the dead frightened him more than we ever did.

villager_spared_line.fallback: You spared a raider for the truth? Then bring me what he named. If the proof exists, I will hear it before I judge you.

return.fallback: So the witness is gone, and truth with him. I will not pretend this sits well.

reward.fallback: Take this, though it feels less like payment and more like hush-money. If the champion lied, we may have just buried the last voice that could prove it.

done.fallback: The witness is dead. The village still cheers the champion, but the sound has soured.
